body: This is super-exciting! One note is that in general we might want to move some of these to https://resources.whatwg.org/standard.css, so they'll apply to all WHATWG specs. But we can worry about that later; it's quite reasonable to prototype in this repo.

There still seems to be a lot of whitespace on the sides:

![2016-03-06 2](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/617481/13557379/32ee2a7c-e3bd-11e5-999f-31ab4dd72dc9.png)
Sorry, my screenshot was from before I incorporated your changes (my build failed for unrelated reasons and I didn't notice). It's much better after!!

>  Fingerprint icon covers the text as well as caniuse table 

I think it would be OK to hide fingerprint icon and caniuse on mobile. (Or at least default caniuse to collapsed.)

there are still whitespace on pages with big tables for sure :disappointed: 

> I think it would be OK to hide fingerprint icon and caniuse on mobile. (Or at least default caniuse to collapsed.)

ok I will work on it.

Another thing worth fixing up is the top links in the nav. Here is what I came up with with a few tweaks in web inspector:

![2016-03-06 7](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/617481/13557476/1e8b0a3a-e3bf-11e5-8232-d30ab3d75bc3.png)

I added `width: 45%` to `#head nav > div > a`, `display: inline` to `#head nav > div`, `text-align: left; font-size: small;` to `#head nav`, and `padding: 0` to `#head nav > div > a > * > *`.

Hmm I don't like how warnings are super-indented. If they could behave more similar to notes, I think it would be ideal.

![2016-03-06 9](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/617481/13557525/d7ee1828-e3bf-11e5-8a45-6010c44cf895.png)
It looks like it would be good to remove `float: right` from `img.extra, p.overview` as well (see 12.2.1).

Agreed. I will work on this tomorrow night.
Please post any other concerns you find and I will try to catch up with them.

Another weird thing I've noticed is that "File an issue about the selected text" ends up way offscreen due to [the mobile viewports WTF](http://www.xanthir.com/b4g00). Maybe it should be hidden on mobile, or maybe just putting it on the left instead of the right would be OK.
Do we need to hide fingerprint? Can't we just make it a lot smaller, and somehow make it not overlap caniuse? (I think it can be made smaller on "desktop" also.)

@yuyokk each caniuse div has `<input onclick="toggleStatus(this)" value="⋰" type="button">` which toggles a "wrapped" class on the div.

Maybe what could be done is the mobile stylesheet could invert the meaning so that `:not(.wrapped)` does what `.wrapped` does currently, and vice-versa.
This makes sense. Will do that.

OK, this LGTM. @yuyokk, would you mind going the extra mile and helping us split this into:
- Things that override parts of standard.css, or could be applied to every spec (like the .img-logo class), which should go as a PR against https://github.com/whatwg/resources.whatwg.org/blob/master/standard.css (preferably with some grouping to make it clear what the overrides are)
- Things that override parts of the HTML-specific stylesheet, which should stay in this PR?
@domenic sure, will do.

I think it's slightly weird to have the caniuse boxes be inversely collapsed when resizing the window to flip between breakpoints. I would prefer a "default" state that is collapsed on small screens and not collapsed on big screens, and clicking the button would switch to collapsed or not collapsed based on whether it is collapsed, and have that state be maintained when crossing a breakpoint.

That probably involves changing what `toggleStatus` does, and I'm fine with not blocking this PR on tweaking this. I could also be convinced that this is a non-issue... :)

> I think it's slightly weird to have the caniuse boxes be inversely collapsed when resizing the window to flip between breakpoints. I would prefer a "default" state that is collapsed on small screens and not collapsed on big screens, and clicking the button would switch to collapsed or not collapsed based on whether it is collapsed, and have that state be maintained when crossing a breakpoint.

I kind of think it's better as-is, actually. Most people don't collapse the boxes. When you resize your browser window to be smaller (e.g. half-screen), you probably start getting annoyed by the boxes and having to collapse them one by one. Having them all flip at once and then become opt-in on smaller screens makes a lot of sense to me.

> So we probably should get bigger @media breakpoint, as an example bootstrap uses 767px = 47.9375em.
> Please let me know what you think about this.

Good catch. I'd be willing to use 767px (don't bother with ems) unless there's some better best practice here.

This looks really usable to me at this point. Been looking at output from this branch with my Galaxy S4 for a while now and have yet to find any improvements to suggest in the current state of the output.
@domenic will you please check the updated commit.
@yuyokk looks really good to me. Maybe we can have @zcorpan work on the tri-state thing in a followup PR? If he's OK with that I'll merge both your PRs.
@domenic sure, thanks. Also I'm happy to work on any other concerns for a mobile layout.
OK with me to merge
Merged at 055f54045075922ad15938f01da24080cb5a3c34. Amazing work; thank you so much!

In https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/2106 I instead made them not be collapsed in the narrow layout, but instead move it mostly out of view.
